title: Sub-Scope Document Editing Delivery
summary: supply an explicit parent or sub-scope document target to the existing source and metadata editors while keeping the public manifest minimal
content_html:
Sub-Scope Document Editing Delivery

Complete Result

On a configured sub-scope report, the ordinary Source action edits the parent report document and a separate subdoc Source action edits the currently displayed, validated sub-scope document.

The existing Edit metadata action edits the current rendered target: the parent report on its list view or the validated sub-scope document on its detail view. The sub-scope modal retains every existing editable field except Parent, including non-viewable.

The manage report lists every sub-scope document and shows the existing Status and non-viewable icons from a compact management-only inventory. The public report continues to receive only its minimal public manifest and shows neither icon.

Both Source actions supply an explicit target. The existing Markdown source editor never derives its target from the displayed document. Source mode has an explicit Return to doc action instead of using either Source action as a toggle.

Control-state contract

Rendered report list:

  • Edit metadata supplies the parent report target;
  • parent report Source is enabled;
  • subdoc Source is disabled; and
  • Return to doc is unavailable.

Rendered valid subdoc detail:

  • Edit metadata supplies the validated sub-scope target;
  • parent report Source remains enabled and supplies the parent doc_id;
  • subdoc Source is enabled and supplies the configured sub_scope and displayed subdoc; and
  • Return to doc is unavailable.

Markdown source:

  • Edit metadata is unavailable;
  • both source-entry actions are visible and disabled;
  • Return to doc is enabled;
  • Save/Rebuild and all existing registered source-editor actions keep their current availability rules; and
  • the toolbar does not permit switching source targets inside a dirty editor.

An unknown, unlisted, loading, or failed subdoc never enables subdoc Source or targets Edit metadata. The report announces valid rendered-detail state through an explicit management integration boundary; toolbar code does not infer validity by scraping report markup or trusting the URL parameter alone.

Explicit managed document target

Source mode and Edit metadata each receive exactly one required target:

parent target:    { scope, doc_id }
sub-scope target: { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }

Neither workflow falls back to selected-document state, displayed payload, doc, or subdoc. Ordinary non-report editing also supplies its target explicitly.

The source target remains fixed for the mounted editor session. Read, rebuild, and Open in VS Code use it. Add image, Add file, Add catalogue token, token inspection/editing, and future registered contributions act through the same active editor context rather than resolving another document.

Edit metadata loads the full record through the local management service using the supplied target. It does not hydrate from the minimal public manifest or compact public by-ID payload.

Public and manage list data remain separate. Public mode receives publicly eligible { doc_id, title } records. Manage mode receives all sub-scope documents with doc_id, title, ui_status, and viewable in one local inventory rather than issuing one by-ID request per row.

Route and return behavior

Entering either source action does not rewrite the document route. For example, editing the subdoc at:

/docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=d-20260624-204534-0d6ae2

preserves both doc and subdoc.

Successful Save/Rebuild retains the current source-editor behavior of returning to rendered view. Return to doc requests the same rendered mode without changing the route and reuses the existing unsaved-change prompt. Browser Back/Forward continues to own report detail state, not source target state.

Opening or saving Edit metadata also preserves the route. A successful subdoc metadata save refreshes the displayed detail and the manifest row when an existing manifest field changes, without selecting the subdoc in the parent index.

Service and rebuild boundary

  • Source read, rebuild, and open requests accept optional sub_scope alongside scope and doc_id.
  • Metadata read and POST /docs/update-metadata accept the same explicit target.
  • An absent sub_scope preserves the current parent-scope behavior exactly.
  • A present sub_scope must identify a configured one-level child of scope; the service resolves only that child document root.
  • The requested doc_id must exist in that sub-scope and match its source front matter.
  • Rebuild preserves the current revision, timestamp, atomic-write, suppression, diagnostics, and activity contracts while invoking the targeted sub-scope document and search builders.
  • The sub-scope metadata request supports Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and viewable. It omits parent_id; the service rejects that field for a sub-scope target and never introduces or changes sub-scope parentage.
  • Metadata hydration reads full source front matter locally. It does not expand the public manifest beyond its existing minimal record contract.
  • The local management inventory includes all sub-scope documents and the two fields required for existing Status/non-viewable icons. It is not copied to the public projection.
  • A viewable change retains the existing visibility contract and refreshes the local management inventory and public eligibility without adding viewable to public manifest rows.
  • Successful subdoc rebuild refreshes the by-ID detail payload and remounts the report detail without changing parent index selection.
  • Invalid or unavailable targets fail before source access and leave rendered state recoverable.

In Scope

  • Add the subdoc Source and Return to doc toolbar controls.
  • Convert the current Source control from a rendered/source toggle into a one-way explicit-target entry action.
  • Project the exact control states above.
  • Let the mounted report publish validated subdoc detail state to the management layer through a narrow callback or event contract.
  • Supply explicit targets to both editing workflows and retain the source target for one editor session.
  • Make the existing Edit metadata action target the parent report on list view and the displayed subdoc on a validated detail view.
  • Hydrate a full sub-scope source record without projecting management metadata into public payloads.
  • Supply one compact manage-only inventory containing all identities, ui_status, and viewable, and render the existing Status/non-viewable icons in manage report rows.
  • Present the existing metadata modal without Parent for a sub-scope target, while preserving Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and non-viewable.
  • Extend metadata mutation and targeted reload behavior for optional sub_scope.
  • Extend the source client, adapter, resolver, rebuild, open-source, activity, and rendered-refresh boundaries for optional sub_scope.
  • Preserve all current source-editor controls and contribution contracts.
  • Add focused service, control-state, module-integration, and route/request evidence.

Not In Scope

  • Changing the public report UI or exposing source controls publicly.
  • Selecting sub-scope documents in the parent index.
  • A second editor, reduced subdoc editor, or report-owned write form.
  • Sub-scope document create, delete, move, transfer, Recent, or global search adoption.
  • Encoding source mode or source target as a new URL parameter.
  • Changing semantic-token syntax or Catalogue target behavior.
  • Publishing or rendering subdoc ui_status; that remains the separate low-priority detail-header enhancement recorded by the parent feature.

These are inspection starting points. Preserve the shared/public report runtime boundary and confirm the exact rendered-detail reload owner before editing it.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: proposed. The product and target contracts are settled, but implementation has not started. SDE-0 through SDE-6 are the delivery sequence.

Next checkpoint: SDE-0 only.

Review rule: complete one phase, record its evidence beneath that phase, and stop for review before starting the next phase. A passing sample proves only the named boundary; it does not advance later phases automatically.

[ ] SDE-0 — Freeze The Explicit-Target Contract And Authority Map

  • [ ] Trace the current rendered/source toggle, selected-document fallback, Edit metadata hydration/save, report-detail state, and rendered reload paths from their UI controls to their service owners.
  • [ ] Record one normalized target shape used by both editing workflows: { scope, doc_id } for a parent document and { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } for a configured sub-scope document.
  • [ ] Identify the single owner that validates a displayed subdoc, the single owner that retains the mounted source target, and the single owner that remounts rendered detail after a targeted rebuild.
  • [ ] Add pure contract fixtures for parent, valid sub-scope, unlisted subdoc, unknown sub-scope, mismatched front-matter identity, loading, and failed detail states.
  • [ ] Capture focused baseline evidence for ordinary parent source editing, metadata editing, dirty return, stale revision, source-editor contributions, public sub-scope manifest shape, and report navigation.
  • [ ] Confirm the maintained files and lowest stable tests for every later phase; revise Likely Authority where inspection disproves a starting point.

Checkpoint / review gate: no runtime behavior changes. Review the exact target normalizer/resolver owner, report-to-management integration seam, rendered-detail reload owner, maintained test list, and green parent-behavior baseline before SDE-1.

[ ] SDE-1 — Add Managed Target Resolution And Inventory

  • [ ] Add one server-side managed-document target resolver that accepts the two approved shapes and returns a confined source document plus its parent scope and optional configured sub-scope.
  • [ ] Preserve current parent resolution when sub_scope is absent. When it is present, require a configured one-level child, resolve only that child's source root, require the requested source file, and verify front-matter doc_id.
  • [ ] Reject blank, unknown, unlisted, mismatched, nested, or path-escaping targets before source read or mutation.
  • [ ] Add one compact management-only sub-scope inventory containing every configured sub-scope document, including non-viewable records, with exactly doc_id, title, ui_status, and viewable.
  • [ ] Keep the public manifest restricted to publicly eligible { doc_id, title } records and keep compact public by-ID payloads unchanged.
  • [ ] Add focused resolver, confinement, inventory, and public-projection tests for repository and external-local source roots.

Checkpoint / review gate: direct service evidence proves valid parent and sub-scope resolution, every invalid-target rejection, complete manage inventory, and byte-equivalent public payload shapes. No source or metadata UI is wired before review.

[ ] SDE-2 — Make Source Editing Target-Aware

  • [ ] Change the source client and adapter to accept one explicit target rather than a bare doc_id plus ambient scope; include sub_scope in source read, rebuild, and Open in VS Code requests only for a sub-scope target.
  • [ ] Mount the approved target once in source-editor state and use it for the complete session. Remove selected, active, displayed, URL doc, and URL subdoc fallbacks from source entry and source-file actions.
  • [ ] Extend source read, source rebuild, and open-source services through the shared managed target resolver.
  • [ ] Route a sub-scope Save/Rebuild through the configured sub-scope document and search builders while preserving atomic write, source revision, timestamp, suppression, diagnostics, and activity contracts.
  • [ ] Keep Add image, Add file, Add catalogue token, token Info/editing, diagram source, and other registered contributions on the mounted editor adapter; do not add a reduced subdoc editor.
  • [ ] Preserve the existing parent request and response contract when sub_scope is absent.
  • [ ] Cover exact request bodies, fixed target retention, contribution context, stale revision, rebuild failure, invalid target, and parent compatibility in focused service and browser-module tests.

Checkpoint / review gate: demonstrate direct parent and sub-scope read/rebuild/open requests plus the fixed-target editor module. Review stale and failure recovery and all registered source-editor contributions before adding new toolbar controls.

[ ] SDE-3 — Make Metadata Editing Target-Aware

  • [ ] Supply Edit metadata with one explicit rendered target and load the full local source record through that target; do not hydrate editable state from a report manifest or compact by-ID payload.
  • [ ] Extend metadata read and POST /docs/update-metadata through the shared resolver while preserving ordinary parent behavior.
  • [ ] Render the sub-scope modal with Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and non-viewable, but without Parent or a hidden parent fallback.
  • [ ] Omit parent_id from every sub-scope request and reject any sub-scope mutation that supplies it without writing.
  • [ ] Rebuild only the targeted sub-scope detail and affected existing manifest/search projections. Preserve the local inventory and public eligibility behavior when viewable changes without exposing it publicly.
  • [ ] Add planner/service tests for every editable field, no-op behavior, parent rejection, timestamp/revision behavior, non-viewable inclusion, public eligibility changes, and ordinary parent compatibility.
  • [ ] Add modal/workflow tests proving full-record hydration, the exact sub-scope field set, and absence of displayed/selected-document fallback.

Checkpoint / review gate: review one focused parent request and the complete sub-scope metadata matrix, including rejected parent_id, manage inventory refresh, and unchanged public schemas, before report and toolbar wiring.

[ ] SDE-4 — Publish Validated Report State And Project Controls

  • [ ] Add a narrow optional report-to-management callback or event that publishes a validated rendered subdoc target only after a listed by-ID detail has loaded successfully.
  • [ ] Clear that target on list view, navigation start, unknown or unlisted subdoc, load failure, report unmount, and scope/document change.
  • [ ] Keep the shared/public report runtime read-only. Consume the management inventory and render existing Status/non-viewable icons only when the manage host explicitly supplies it.
  • [ ] Project the exact control-state matrix from this delivery: parent Source, subdoc Source, Edit metadata, and Return to doc across rendered list, rendered valid detail, invalid/loading detail, and Markdown source.
  • [ ] Convert Source entry from a toggle to a one-way action. Keep both source entry controls visible but disabled in source mode and make Return to doc its only explicit toolbar exit.
  • [ ] Route parent Source from the parent report target even while detail is displayed. Route subdoc Source and Edit metadata only from the validated management target; never infer either from report markup or URL parameters.
  • [ ] Add pure control-projection and report-module tests for every state, public/manage inventory separation, accessible labels, and no dirty-editor target switching.

Checkpoint / review gate: review the complete pure state matrix and mounted report module with no mutations. Confirm invalid/loading states remain disabled, public rendering remains unchanged, and each enabled control emits the exact target before integrated route work.

[ ] SDE-5 — Complete Return, Refresh, And Route Integration

  • [ ] Preserve scope, parent doc, and existing subdoc route parameters when entering source mode, opening/saving metadata, returning, or rebuilding.
  • [ ] Reuse the existing dirty-state confirmation for Return to doc; Cancel keeps the fixed source session, while confirmed return remounts the unchanged rendered route.
  • [ ] After successful sub-scope source or metadata rebuild, refresh the targeted by-ID detail and affected manage inventory/manifest state, then remount the detail without selecting it in the parent index.
  • [ ] Preserve current successful Save/Rebuild return behavior and recoverable stale-revision, service-unavailable, invalid-target, and rebuild-failure states.
  • [ ] Keep Browser Back/Forward authoritative for report list/detail navigation and keep source target state out of the URL.
  • [ ] Add direct request/response coverage and one synthetic, test-owned manage-route smoke covering parent Source while detail is displayed, subdoc Source, metadata field shape, Return/dirty handling, targeted refresh, and invalid detail disablement.
  • [ ] Add a public-route assertion proving that management inventory, icons, and source controls are absent.

Checkpoint / review gate: review the durable manage-route smoke and exact request log. Confirm no persistent fixture mutation, no parent index selection change, no route drift, and no public-surface change before closeout.

[ ] SDE-6 — Verify, Document, And Close

  • [ ] Run focused target-resolver, source-service, metadata-service, builder, inventory/public-projection, control-state, report-module, source-editor, and route/request tests.
  • [ ] Run maintained source lint, the complete Docs Viewer smoke profile, the relevant docs/generated-output checks, and git diff --check; report exact counts and scopes rather than subsystem-wide claims from a subset.
  • [ ] Manually review the rendered report list, valid and invalid detail, parent Source, subdoc Source, metadata modal, dirty Return, successful rebuild, non-viewable inventory row, and public report in a configured local sub-scope.
  • [ ] Verify source and metadata actions cannot resolve an unlisted ID or escape the configured child root, and that every source-editor contribution uses the mounted target.
  • [ ] Verify the parent report remains selected, routes remain stable, public manifests remain minimal, and subdocs remain absent from parent Index, Recent, and global search.
  • [ ] Update the feature parent and the durable destinations named below with the shipped contracts; remove delivery chronology from current-state docs.
  • [ ] Independently inspect the final diff and evidence before marking every phase and this delivery done.

Checkpoint / review gate: user acceptance of the manual UI, complete green evidence, current-state durable docs, and final diff review. Only then mark SDE-0 through SDE-6 complete and change ui_status from proposed to done.

Completion And Evidence

  • Parent Source always reads the supplied parent report doc_id, even while a subdoc is displayed.
  • Subdoc Source is enabled only for a successfully displayed listed detail and sends the exact { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }.
  • The source editor has no selected/displayed-document fallback.
  • Edit metadata receives the parent target on report list view and the exact sub-scope target on a valid detail view, with no selected/displayed fallback.
  • The sub-scope modal contains every existing editable metadata field except Parent; its request contains no parent_id.
  • A sub-scope metadata request that supplies parent_id is rejected without a write.
  • Full metadata hydration comes from the local source record and does not add fields to the public manifest or compact public by-ID payload.
  • Manage report rows show existing Status/non-viewable icons from one local inventory that also retains non-viewable documents.
  • The public manifest contains only publicly eligible { doc_id, title } records, and the public report renders neither icon.
  • Both source-entry controls are disabled in source mode and Return to doc is the only explicit toolbar exit.
  • Dirty return, successful rebuild, stale revision, and rebuild failure retain their current recoverable behavior.
  • Save/Rebuild, Add image, Add file, Add catalogue token, token Info, and Open in VS Code operate on the active supplied target.
  • Parent source requests remain byte-for-byte compatible apart from internal target construction.
  • Sub-scope source requests cannot escape the configured sub-scope root or resolve an unlisted ID.
  • Title and other metadata changes rebuild the targeted detail and any affected existing manifest/search projection; viewable retains its public visibility behavior without becoming a manifest field.
  • A subdoc rebuild refreshes the detail without adding it to the parent index, Recent, or global search.
  • Focused pure control-state, source-service, metadata-service, builder, and public-projection tests; direct request/response checks; module wiring checks; one durable manage-route smoke; manual toolbar/modal/dirty-state review; and git diff --check support only this delivery.

Durable Destinations

Transfer the explicit target and toolbar behavior to the maintained Docs Viewer source-editing documentation. Transfer metadata mutation and visibility behavior to Source Mutation Endpoints and Viewable field. Transfer configured sub-scope detail/reload behavior to Embedded Detail Documents and the report integration boundary to Reports.
